title: A bigger bank doesn't spread use
statement: Growing an adaptive bank doesn't by itself spread use across it.
example: When staged expansions took one bank from 650 to 786 items, never-used items rose from 241 to 289, about the same share, and over-exposed items stayed at 38.
detail: Across a reading assessment's simulation runs on its 650-item bank, never-used items fell from 322 to 241 and items used in more than 30% of sessions from 41 to 38 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`). Staged expansions then added 92 edge items extending the floor and ceiling, 18 above the ceiling and 26 for under-covered standards (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`), and on the 786-item bank never-used items rose to 289, about the same share as 241 of 650, while over-exposed items stayed at 38. The package records that use remains concentrated and that balancing exposure across bands is the open follow-up (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`).
against: The largest single exposure did fall as the bank grew, from 0.909 to 0.709 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`). Most added items sit at the floor and ceiling, which adaptive selection rarely reaches because it concentrates use near the middle of the population (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/04_CONCURRENT_VALIDITY_PLAN.md`), so the result says little about adding items where use is concentrated.

evidence.quote: | Sim 5 never-used items | 322/650 | 256/650 | 241/650 | **289/786** | ↓ | rose with the larger bank; per-band exposure balancing is the open follow-up |
| Sim 5 over-exposed (>30%) | 41/650 | 39/650 | 38/650 | **38/786** | ↓ | max exposure 0.709; exposure-aware scoring the open follow-up |
| +92 | Floor extension to ~RIT 155; ceiling to 235 | Merged; harness-validated |
| +44 (26 + 18) | 26 standard-gap items closing nine under-target standards (see §5 note); 18 G5 super-ceiling items at **RIT 231–250**
26 standard-gap items closing nine under-target standards + 18 G5 super-ceiling items at RIT 231–250

289 items were never used in the v4 run — never-used rose from 241/650 at v3 as the bank grew to 786 items; randomesque top-5 selection in both selection phases spreads exposure, but utilization remains concentrated and per-band exposure balancing is the open follow-up
max item exposure fell to 0.709 (from 0.909 at v3)
Natural CAT exposure concentrates responses at the population center: tail-band items would see only ~50–100 responses each under proportional usage — below the calibration floor.
